sections.title: Personal data
paragraphs: Data collected: when you use the contact form, your name, e-mail address, the reason for your message and the message itself. No other personal data is collected.
Purpose and legal basis: this data is used only to reply to you and follow up on your request, based on the legitimate interest in handling the requests received.

Recipients: your data is never sold or used for marketing. The form is sent through Web3Forms, a service that forwards the message to my mailbox (Gmail, Google). These providers act as processors and may process data outside the European Union, with appropriate safeguards.
Retention: messages are kept for 1 year after the last exchange, then deleted.
As with any website, the host may record technical data (such as your IP address) to keep the site secure and working properly.

Your rights: you can access, correct or delete your data, restrict or object to its processing and ask for its portability by writing to <mail>{{email}}</mail>. You can also lodge a complaint with the French data protection authority, the CNIL (<cnil>www.cnil.fr</cnil>).

sections.title: Cookies
paragraphs: This website uses no cookies or tracking tools. It only stores in your browser the language you choose, so the site opens in that language on your next visit. This information is never shared and you can delete it in your browser settings.

interfaceWebApp.seoTitle: Interface Web App — Flexis case study · Karol Giraldo
interfaceWebApp.seoDescription: How I designed Flexis Interface, a web platform that turns fleet data into clear daily decisions for fleet managers.

hero.title:
From fleet data to
clear daily decisions
hero.lead: A new platform built from scratch to help fleet teams make sense of their data and know what to do next.
hero.videoLabel: Screen recording of the Flexis Interface dashboard: fleet availability, mileage consumption, alerts and a live map of vehicles.

problem.title: The problem
problem.lead: Fleet teams have more data than ever, but no clear way to act on it.

solution.title: The solution
solution.lead: A new platform that turns fleet data into clear priorities and actions.

cards.title: Fleet Overview
cards.text: What needs attention today, at a glance.
cards.alt: Flexis Interface home dashboard: fleet availability, mileage consumption, alerts requiring attention and a map of vehicles on route.

cards.title: Vehicle detail
cards.alt: Vehicle detail screen: check-in and check-out, monthly mileage, annual consumption, battery level and vehicle location.

cards.title: Actionable workflows
cards.text: From alert to action in a few steps.
cards.alt: Notification Center with the list of fleet alerts and an open panel for a low tire pressure alert, with the recommended action.

context.label: (Context)
context.title: Electric fleets bring more data, and more to manage.
context.lead:
On top of location, managers now track charging, battery, maintenance, availability and costs.
Flexis set out to build a new product for this shift.

research.title: Research
research.lead: Many tools track the fleet, none help decide what to do next.
research.text: Before designing anything, I interviewed fleet business experts and benchmarked tools like Geotab and Samsara. Three gaps stood out.
research.conclusion: As a result, teams jump between tools and end up sorting it out in Excel.

gaps.text: Data without priorities: everything is tracked and reported, but nothing shows what matters most.
gaps.alt: Fleet dashboard widgets side by side: a driving smoothness score chart, 10% of vehicles charging and 1 of 10 charge points in use.

gaps.text: Scattered across tools: vehicle, driver and charging information live in separate services.
gaps.alt: An electric van surrounded by separate cards: a wallbox at the Lyon hub with two available charge points, and 3 of 10 charge points available.

gaps.text: One user only: most products serve the Fleet Manager alone.
gaps.alt: Role picker with Fleet Manager selected; the other roles, Dispatcher, Fleet Advisor and Financial Manager, fade into the background.

fleetAdvisor.title: Fleet Advisor
fleetAdvisor.text: Provides advice and support on fleet strategy

financialManager.title: Financial Manager
financialManager.text: Oversees financial planning for the fleet

question.text: How might we turn a large amount of <muted>fragmented fleet data</muted> into a simple experience that helps teams know what to do next?

process.title: Process
process.lead: No existing product: every module started from a business goal.

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: Expert interviews and benchmark to define each module before designing it.
steps.alt: A fleet advisor in a high-visibility vest holding a tablet, in front of a board about monthly on-site visits.

steps.title: Define
steps.text: With Product and Business, we decided what to build first and mapped the flows for the first release.
steps.alt: Workshop board with priorities ranked high, medium and low, the problem statement, hypotheses and research goals.

steps.title: Design & validate
steps.text: I reviewed wireframes with developers, experts and beta testers before moving to high-fidelity UI.
steps.alt: Meeting room with the User Management screen projected on a large screen during a review session.

slides.title:
Not all data
deserves the same
visibility.

items.title: Audit
items.text: Mapped every data point from vehicles, telematics and operations.

items.title: Prioritize
items.text: Ranked information by urgency and required action, separating what is informative from what needs attention.

items.title: Structure
items.text: Fleet overview → vehicle detail → next action.

slides.alt: Flexis screens layered on top of each other: the fleet management table, the filter panel and a vehicle detail page with mileage and consumption.

slides.title:
One consistent way to
read and act, across
every module.
slides.text: With no existing UI to rely on, I built the design system alongside the product. Recurring patterns (statuses, alerts, filters, actions) became reusable components, so the same signal always looks and behaves the same, and new modules don’t add complexity.
slides.alt: Design system components: buttons, checkbox, KPI cards, alerts, status tags and a mileage progress bar with a warning.

final.title: Final Thoughts

stats.label: product modules designed end to end

final.summary: A platform that turns scattered fleet data into clear daily actions, designed in one year and ready for development before Flexis was acquired.
final.photoAlt: A fleet manager in a high-visibility vest working at her desk, with the Flexis planning screen on her monitor.

driverApp.seoTitle: Driver App — Flexis case study · Karol Giraldo
driverApp.seoDescription: How I designed the Flexis Driver App, a mobile app that takes urban delivery drivers from vehicle pickup to mission done.

hero.title:
From vehicle pickup
to mission done, in
one app
hero.lead: A mobile app built from scratch to help urban delivery drivers start their day faster, drive better and stay connected to their fleet.
hero.videoLabel: Screen recording of the Flexis Driver App: finding the assigned vehicle on a map and starting navigation to it.

problem.title: The problem
problem.lead: Drivers had no single tool for their day, and no clear way to pair with their vehicle.
problem.detail: Vehicles were tracked live in Interface, but there was no reliable way to know who was driving each one, and when.

solution.title: The solution
solution.lead: One app for the driver’s day, starting with a simple vehicle pairing.

cards.title: Vehicle pairing
cards.text: Scan the QR code or enter the VIN number to start a mission, or unlock the vehicle with a virtual key.
cards.alt: Vehicle pairing screen: the camera scans the vehicle’s VIN number, with a field to enter the vehicle code manually.

cards.title: Video check-in & check-out
cards.text: The driver films the vehicle, and an integrated inspection service completes the report.
cards.alt: Video check-in screen: the driver films the van from the outside while recording.

cards.title: Smart daily mission
cards.text: Routes and stop order optimized to use less energy.
cards.alt: Mission navigation screen: turn-by-turn directions on a night map, the next stop and buttons to call the customer or report an incident.

context.label: (Context)
context.title: Last-mile delivery runs on tight schedules and shared vans.
context.lead: In last-mile logistics, several drivers share the same vans, rounds are tight, and electric vehicles add a new constraint: range. Flexis built this app for delivery drivers across Europe.

research.title: Research
research.text: Working with business experts, we mapped a full shift, from depot to last delivery, and found three gaps:
research.conclusion: The result: low driver engagement and lower fleet productivity.

gaps.text: Fragmented tools: drivers managed their deliveries across different tools, without real-time information.
gaps.alt: An electric van between three status cards: vehicle not connected, vehicle connected and ready to check in, and vehicle ready to start the day.

gaps.text: Not designed for drivers: existing solutions lacked the basics of a driver’s day, like a smooth onboarding and secure vehicle access.
gaps.alt: The Driver App home screen with turn-by-turn directions, a van seen from above and a “Find Your Vehicle” card.

gaps.text: No driver–vehicle pairing: vans were tracked, but there was no clear way to know who was driving each one, and when.
gaps.alt: An electric van in front of a “Find Your Vehicle” card and a link icon.

question.text: How might we give last-mile drivers <muted>one intuitive app that simplifies their daily operations</muted>, from vehicle access to the end of the round?

process.title: Process
process.lead: No existing product: every module started from a business goal.

steps.title: Map
steps.text: story mapping turned the business goals into epics and user stories, from driver onboarding to route monitoring.
steps.alt: Story mapping board for mission planning, with the user needs, the vehicle types and the unassigned routes.

steps.title: Prioritize
steps.text: with Product and Business, we used MoSCoW to define the MVP and the next release (MMP).
steps.alt: A designer arranging sticky notes on a glass wall, under the steps of the driver’s journey: profile, vehicle, location, stats and planning.

steps.title: Design & validate
steps.text: I mapped the user flows and validated low-fi mockups before development.
steps.alt: A driver in a high-visibility vest holding a phone with the Driver App’s “Session Completed” screen.
